text.en: Meena squeezed lemon on her turmeric-stained cloth and the colour changed. "Acids change colours," she said.

Substances with a sour taste are acids, and bases are substances that ionise in water to give hydroxide ions (OH-) according to Arrhenius. Bases soluble in water are alkalis. Acids are classed by basicity as monobasic, dibasic and tribasic according to the replaceable hydrogen ions per molecule.
Indicators such as litmus show acids and bases by colour change. When an acid and a base react a neutral product, a salt, forms together with water, and this is a neutralisation reaction, for example HCl + NaOH gives NaCl + H2O. Sulphuric acid is called the king of chemicals because many compounds are made from it.
Salts are classed as normal, acidic and basic, and some crystallise with water of crystallisation, as in copper sulphate. The strength of an acid or base is measured on the pH scale, and salts can be identified by simple tests.

text.en: An acid and a base react to give a salt and water.
The salt here is sodium chloride.

requiredIdeas.en: Those that dissolve are called alkalis.
